edition: 2025 civics test (128 questions) — for Form N-400 applications filed on or after October 20, 2025; still the current version in October 2026. Applicants who filed before October 20, 2025 take the 2008 civics test (100 questions).

exam.rules: The civics test is an oral test given by a USCIS officer at the naturalization interview. For applications filed on or after October 20, 2025, the officer asks up to 20 of the 128 official questions and you must answer 12 correctly; the officer stops once you have 12 correct or 9 incorrect answers. Questions about office holders (President, Vice President, Speaker, Chief Justice) must be answered with the person serving at the time of your interview, and some questions depend on where you live (your senators, representative, governor and state capital). If you are 65 or older and have been a lawful permanent resident for 20 or more years (65/20 special consideration), you study only the 20 starred questions, may take the test in your language, are asked 10 of them and need 6 correct. Applicants who filed before October 20, 2025 take the 2008 test instead (up to 10 of 100 questions, 6 correct to pass). If you fail, you get one retest, usually 60–90 days later.

topics.title: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information

questions.q: What is the form of government of the United States?
questions.explain: The United States is a republic. Also accepted: constitution-based federal republic; representative democracy.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 1

questions.q: What is the supreme law of the land?
questions.explain: The (U.S.) Constitution is the supreme law of the land.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 2 (* 65/20)

questions.q: Name one thing the U.S. Constitution does.
options: Sets the federal budget each year
questions.explain: Accepted answers: forms the government; defines powers of government; defines the parts of government; protects the rights of the people.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 3

questions.q: The U.S. Constitution starts with the words “We the People.” What does “We the People” mean?
questions.explain: “We the People” means the people govern themselves. Also accepted: popular sovereignty; consent of the governed; people should govern themselves; (example of) social contract.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 4

questions.q: How are changes made to the U.S. Constitution?
questions.explain: The Constitution is changed through amendments. Also accepted: the amendment process.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 5

questions.q: What does the Bill of Rights protect?
options: The power of Congress to collect taxes
questions.explain: The Bill of Rights protects the basic rights of Americans. Also accepted: the basic rights of people living in the United States.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 6

questions.q: How many amendments does the U.S. Constitution have?
questions.explain: The Constitution has 27 amendments. (The first 10 are the Bill of Rights.)
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 7 (* 65/20)

questions.q: Why is the Declaration of Independence important?
options: It says America is free from British control.
It created the three branches of government.
questions.explain: Also accepted: it says all people are created equal; it identifies inherent rights; it identifies individual freedoms.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 8

questions.q: What founding document said the American colonies were free from Britain?
questions.explain: The Declaration of Independence (1776) said the colonies were free from Britain.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 9

questions.q: Name two important ideas from the Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution.
questions.explain: Accepted answers: equality; liberty; social contract; natural rights; limited government; self-government.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 10

questions.q: The words “Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness” are in what founding document?
questions.explain: These words are in the Declaration of Independence.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 11

questions.q: What is the economic system of the United States?
questions.explain: The U.S. economic system is capitalism. Also accepted: free market economy.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 12 (* 65/20)

questions.q: What is the rule of law?
options: The President can overrule any court.
Only judges must follow the law.
No one is above the law.
questions.explain: Also accepted: everyone must follow the law; leaders must obey the law; government must obey the law.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 13

questions.q: Many documents influenced the U.S. Constitution. Name one.
questions.explain: Also accepted: Declaration of Independence; Federalist Papers; Anti-Federalist Papers; Virginia Declaration of Rights; Fundamental Orders of Connecticut; Mayflower Compact; Iroquois Great Law of Peace.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 14

questions.q: There are three branches of government. Why?
options: So laws can be passed faster
So the President can choose which branch to use
So each state can have its own branch
So one part does not become too powerful
questions.explain: Also accepted: checks and balances; separation of powers.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, A: Principles of American Government, question 15

questions.q: Name the three branches of government.
questions.explain: Also accepted: Congress, president, and the courts.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 16

questions.q: The President of the United States is in charge of which branch of government?
questions.explain: The President leads the executive branch.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 17

questions.q: What part of the federal government writes laws?
questions.explain: Also accepted: (U.S. or national) legislature; legislative branch.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 18

questions.q: What are the two parts of the U.S. Congress?
options: The Senate and the House of Representatives
The Senate and the Supreme Court
The President and the Vice President
The House of Representatives and the Cabinet
questions.explain: Congress is made up of the Senate and the House (of Representatives).
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 19

questions.q: Name one power of the U.S. Congress.
questions.explain: Accepted answers: writes laws; declares war; makes the federal budget. Vetoing bills, appointing judges and commanding the military are powers of the President.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 20 (* 65/20)

questions.q: How many U.S. senators are there?
questions.explain: There are 100 U.S. senators: two from each of the 50 states.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 21

questions.q: How long is a term for a U.S. senator?
questions.explain: A U.S. senator is elected for a six-year term.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 22

questions.q: Official question 23 asks: “Who is one of your state’s U.S. senators now?” Which answer does USCIS accept?
options: The name of either of the two U.S. senators who currently represent your state
The name of your U.S. representative
The name of your state’s governor
The name of any U.S. senator from any state
questions.explain: The answer depends on where you live, so learn the names of your state’s two current senators (senate.gov). D.C. residents and residents of U.S. territories should answer that D.C. (or their territory) has no U.S. senators.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 23 — rewritten: the official answer depends on where the applicant lives

questions.q: How many voting members are in the House of Representatives?
questions.explain: The House has 435 voting members.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 24

questions.q: How long is a term for a member of the House of Representatives?
questions.explain: Members of the House are elected for two-year terms.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 25

questions.q: Why do U.S. representatives serve shorter terms than U.S. senators?
options: To more closely follow public opinion
Because the Constitution limits them to one term
Because the House has fewer members than the Senate
Because representatives are appointed, not elected
questions.explain: Short two-year terms make representatives face voters often, so they more closely follow public opinion.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 26

questions.q: How many senators does each state have?
options: It depends on the state’s population
questions.explain: Every state has two senators. (The number of representatives, not senators, depends on population.)
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 27

questions.q: Why does each state have two senators?
options: Because each state has two political parties
To give the President two advisors from each state
Because states with more people need more senators
questions.explain: Also accepted: the Great Compromise (Connecticut Compromise).
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 28

questions.q: Official question 29 asks: “Name your U.S. representative.” Which answer does USCIS accept?
options: The name of the member of the House who currently represents your congressional district
The name of the Speaker of the House
The name of one of your state’s U.S. senators
The name of your representative in the state legislature
questions.explain: The answer depends on where you live; find your representative at house.gov. Residents of territories with a nonvoting Delegate or Resident Commissioner may name that person, or say the territory has no (voting) representatives in Congress.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 29 — rewritten: the official answer depends on where the applicant lives

questions.q: What is the name of the Speaker of the House of Representatives now?
questions.explain: As of October 2026 the Speaker is Mike Johnson. This answer can change (a new Congress starts in January 2027); give the name of the Speaker serving at the time of your interview and check uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 30 (* 65/20)

questions.q: Who does a U.S. senator represent?
options: Citizens of their congressional district only
questions.explain: Also accepted: people of their state.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 31

questions.q: Who elects U.S. senators?
questions.explain: Senators are elected by the citizens of their state (since the 17th Amendment, 1913).
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 32

questions.q: Who does a member of the House of Representatives represent?
questions.explain: Also accepted: citizens in their district; people from/in their (congressional) district.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 33

questions.q: Who elects members of the House of Representatives?
questions.explain: Representatives are elected by citizens from their (congressional) district.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 34

questions.q: Some states have more representatives than other states. Why?
options: Because they joined the Union earlier
Because of the state’s land area
questions.explain: Also accepted: (because) they have more people; (because) some states have more people.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 35

questions.q: The President of the United States is elected for how many years?
questions.explain: The President is elected for a four-year term.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 36 (* 65/20)

questions.q: The President of the United States can serve only two terms. Why?
questions.explain: Also accepted: to keep the president from becoming too powerful.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 37

questions.q: What is the name of the President of the United States now?
questions.explain: As of October 2026 the President is Donald J. Trump (in office since January 20, 2025). Give the name of the President serving at the time of your interview; check uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 38 (* 65/20)

questions.q: What is the name of the Vice President of the United States now?
questions.explain: As of October 2026 the Vice President is JD Vance (in office since January 20, 2025). Give the name of the Vice President serving at the time of your interview; check uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 39 (* 65/20)

questions.q: If the president can no longer serve, who becomes president?
questions.explain: The Vice President (of the United States) becomes president.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 40

questions.q: Name one power of the president.
questions.explain: Accepted answers: signs bills into law; vetoes bills; enforces laws; Commander in Chief (of the military); chief diplomat; appoints federal judges.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 41

questions.q: Who is Commander in Chief of the U.S. military?
questions.explain: The President (of the United States) is Commander in Chief.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 42

questions.q: Who signs bills to become laws?
questions.explain: The President (of the United States) signs bills into law.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 43

questions.q: Who vetoes bills?
questions.explain: The President (of the United States) vetoes bills.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 44 (* 65/20)

questions.q: Who appoints federal judges?
questions.explain: The President (of the United States) appoints federal judges.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 45

questions.q: The executive branch has many parts. Name one.
questions.explain: Accepted answers: President (of the United States); Cabinet; federal departments and agencies.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 46

questions.q: What does the President’s Cabinet do?
questions.explain: The Cabinet advises the President (of the United States).
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 47

questions.q: What are two Cabinet-level positions?
options: Secretary of State and Attorney General
Speaker of the House and Secretary of State
Senate Majority Leader and Secretary of Labor
questions.explain: Accepted: Attorney General; Secretaries of Agriculture, Commerce, Education, Energy, Health and Human Services, Homeland Security, Housing and Urban Development, the Interior, Labor, State, Transportation, the Treasury, Veterans Affairs, War (Defense); Vice President; EPA and SBA Administrators; CIA Director; OMB Director; Director of National Intelligence; U.S. Trade Representative.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 48

questions.q: Why is the Electoral College important?
options: It decides who is elected president.
It decides who sits on the Supreme Court.
questions.explain: Also accepted: it provides a compromise between the popular election of the president and congressional selection.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 49

questions.q: What is one part of the judicial branch?
questions.explain: Also accepted: federal courts. (The Department of Justice is part of the executive branch.)
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 50

questions.q: What does the judicial branch do?
options: Decides if a law goes against the Constitution
questions.explain: Also accepted: reviews laws; explains laws; resolves disputes (disagreements) about the law.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 51

questions.q: What is the highest court in the United States?
questions.explain: The Supreme Court is the highest court in the United States.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 52 (* 65/20)

questions.q: How many seats are on the Supreme Court?
questions.explain: The Supreme Court has nine seats.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 53

questions.q: How many Supreme Court justices are usually needed to decide a case?
questions.explain: A majority of the nine justices, five, is usually needed to decide a case.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 54

questions.q: How long do Supreme Court justices serve?
questions.explain: Also accepted: lifetime appointment; (until) retirement.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 55

questions.q: Supreme Court justices serve for life. Why?
options: Because the Constitution requires them to be elected
So they can later run for President
Because no one can replace them
questions.explain: Also accepted: to limit outside (political) influence.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 56

questions.q: Who is the Chief Justice of the United States now?
questions.explain: As of October 2026 the Chief Justice is John G. Roberts, Jr. (since 2005). Give the name of the Chief Justice serving at the time of your interview; check uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 57

questions.q: Name one power that is only for the federal government.
questions.explain: Also accepted: mint coins; declare war; create an army; make treaties; set foreign policy. The other options are powers of the states.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 58

questions.q: Name one power that is only for the states.
questions.explain: Also accepted: provide schooling and education; provide protection (police); provide safety (fire departments); approve zoning and land use.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 59

questions.q: What is the purpose of the 10th Amendment?
options: It gives women the right to vote.
It limits the President to two terms.
Powers not given to the federal government belong to the states or to the people.
questions.explain: The 10th Amendment reserves powers not given to the federal government to the states or to the people.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 60

questions.q: Official question 61 asks: “Who is the governor of your state now?” Which answer does USCIS accept?
options: The name of your state’s capital city
The name of the person serving as governor of your state at the time of your interview
The name of your state’s first governor
The name of the President of the United States
questions.explain: The answer depends on where you live, so learn your state’s current governor (see your state’s official website). D.C. residents should answer that D.C. does not have a governor. This is one of the 20 questions for the 65/20 special consideration.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 61 (* 65/20) — rewritten: the official answer depends on where the applicant lives

questions.q: Official question 62 asks: “What is the capital of your state?” Which answer does USCIS accept?
options: The capital city of the state where you live (for example, Albany for New York)
The largest city in your state (for example, New York City for New York)
The city where you were born
questions.explain: The answer depends on where you live; the capital is often not the largest city. D.C. residents should answer that D.C. is not a state and has no capital; residents of U.S. territories should name the territory’s capital.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, B: System of Government, question 62 — rewritten: the official answer depends on where the applicant lives

questions.q: There are four amendments to the U.S. Constitution about who can vote. Describe one of them.
options: Only citizens who own land can vote.
Citizens eighteen (18) and older can vote.
Citizens must pay a poll tax to vote.
questions.explain: Also accepted: you don’t have to pay (a poll tax) to vote; any citizen can vote (women and men can vote); a male citizen of any race (can vote).
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, C: Rights and Responsibilities, question 63

questions.q: Who can vote in federal elections, run for federal office, and serve on a jury in the United States?
options: Anyone age 18 or older living in the U.S.
questions.explain: Only citizens (of the United States) can do these things.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, C: Rights and Responsibilities, question 64

questions.q: What are three rights of everyone living in the United States?
options: Freedom of speech, freedom of religion, freedom of assembly
Freedom of assembly, the right to run for federal office, freedom of religion
The right to serve on a federal jury, freedom of speech, the right to bear arms
Freedom of speech, the right to vote in federal elections, freedom of religion
questions.explain: Accepted: freedom of expression; freedom of speech; freedom of assembly; freedom to petition the government; freedom of religion; the right to bear arms. Voting, running for federal office and jury service are for citizens only.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, C: Rights and Responsibilities, question 65

questions.q: What do we show loyalty to when we say the Pledge of Allegiance?
questions.explain: Also accepted: the flag.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, C: Rights and Responsibilities, question 66 (* 65/20)

questions.q: Name two promises that new citizens make in the Oath of Allegiance.
options: Defend the Constitution and join a political party
Give up loyalty to other countries and defend the Constitution
Vote in every election and join a political party
Give up loyalty to other countries and never travel abroad
questions.explain: Accepted: give up loyalty to other countries; defend the (U.S.) Constitution; obey the laws of the United States; serve in the military (if needed); serve the nation (if needed); be loyal to the United States.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, C: Rights and Responsibilities, question 67

questions.q: How can people become United States citizens?
options: Live in the United States for one year
Buy property in the United States
questions.explain: Also accepted: be born in the United States, under the conditions set by the 14th Amendment; derive citizenship (under conditions set by Congress).
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, C: Rights and Responsibilities, question 68

questions.q: What are two examples of civic participation in the United States?
options: Get a library card and join a gym
Vote and join a civic group
Buy a car and open a bank account
questions.explain: Accepted: vote; run for office; join a political party; help with a campaign; join a civic or community group; give an elected official your opinion; contact elected officials; support or oppose an issue or policy; write to a newspaper.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, C: Rights and Responsibilities, question 69

questions.q: What is one way Americans can serve their country?
questions.explain: Also accepted: vote; pay taxes; obey the law; run for office; work for local, state, or federal government.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, C: Rights and Responsibilities, question 70

questions.q: Why is it important to pay federal taxes?
options: Only citizens living abroad must pay them
It is optional, so paying is a courtesy
questions.explain: Also accepted: all people pay to fund the federal government; required by the (U.S.) Constitution (16th Amendment); civic duty.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, C: Rights and Responsibilities, question 71

questions.q: It is important for all men age 18 through 25 to register for the Selective Service. Name one reason why.
options: It is required only for women
questions.explain: Also accepted: civic duty; makes the draft fair, if needed.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American Government, C: Rights and Responsibilities, question 72

questions.q: The colonists came to America for many reasons. Name one.
options: To serve in the British army
questions.explain: Also accepted: freedom; political liberty; economic opportunity; escape persecution.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 73

questions.q: Who lived in America before the Europeans arrived?
questions.explain: Also accepted: Native Americans.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 74 (* 65/20)

questions.q: What group of people was taken and sold as slaves?
questions.explain: Also accepted: people from Africa.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 75

questions.q: What war did the Americans fight to win independence from Britain?
questions.explain: Also accepted: the (American) Revolutionary War; War for (American) Independence.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 76

questions.q: Name one reason why the Americans declared independence from Britain.
options: The colonists wanted to keep the Articles of Confederation
Britain gave the colonists too many seats in Parliament
The colonists wanted to join France
questions.explain: Also accepted: high taxes; British soldiers stayed in Americans’ houses (quartering); no self-government; Boston Massacre; Boston Tea Party (Tea Act); Stamp Act; Sugar Act; Townshend Acts; Intolerable (Coercive) Acts.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 77

questions.q: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?
questions.explain: (Thomas) Jefferson wrote the Declaration of Independence.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 78 (* 65/20)

questions.q: When was the Declaration of Independence adopted?
questions.explain: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776. (September 17, 1787 is when the Constitution was signed.)
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 79

questions.q: The American Revolution had many important events. Name one.
questions.explain: Also accepted: (Battle of) Bunker Hill; Declaration of Independence; Washington Crossing the Delaware (Battle of Trenton); Valley Forge (Encampment); (Battle of) Yorktown.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 80

questions.q: There were 13 original states. Name five.
options: New Hampshire, New York, Virginia, Georgia, Maryland
Rhode Island, North Carolina, Florida, New York, Delaware
Connecticut, Maine, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, South Carolina
questions.explain: The 13 original states: New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia. Vermont, Maine and Florida joined later.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 81

questions.q: What founding document was written in 1787?
questions.explain: The (U.S.) Constitution was written in 1787.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 82

questions.q: The Federalist Papers supported the passage of the U.S. Constitution. Name one of the writers.
questions.explain: Also accepted: (Alexander) Hamilton; (John) Jay; Publius.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 83

questions.q: Why were the Federalist Papers important?
options: They helped people understand the U.S. Constitution.
questions.explain: Also accepted: they supported passing the (U.S.) Constitution.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 84

questions.q: Benjamin Franklin is famous for many things. Name one.
options: Third president of the United States
First president of the United States
First Postmaster General of the United States
questions.explain: Also accepted: founded the first free public libraries; helped write the Declaration of Independence; inventor; U.S. diplomat.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 85

questions.q: George Washington is famous for many things. Name one.
options: First president of the United States
questions.explain: Also accepted: “Father of Our Country”; General of the Continental Army; President of the Constitutional Convention.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 86 (* 65/20)

questions.q: Thomas Jefferson is famous for many things. Name one.
options: Third president of the United States
First president of the United States
questions.explain: Also accepted: writer of the Declaration of Independence; doubled the size of the U.S. (Louisiana Purchase); first Secretary of State; founded the University of Virginia; writer of the Virginia Statute on Religious Freedom.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 87

questions.q: James Madison is famous for many things. Name one.
options: Writer of the Declaration of Independence
questions.explain: Also accepted: fourth president of the United States; president during the War of 1812; one of the writers of the Federalist Papers.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 88

questions.q: Alexander Hamilton is famous for many things. Name one.
options: Writer of the Declaration of Independence
Third president of the United States
questions.explain: Also accepted: one of the writers of the Federalist Papers; helped establish the First Bank of the United States; aide to General George Washington; member of the Continental Congress.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, A: Colonial Period and Independence, question 89

questions.q: What territory did the United States buy from France in 1803?
questions.explain: The U.S. bought the Louisiana Territory (Louisiana) from France in 1803. Alaska was bought from Russia; Florida came from Spain.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, B: 1800s, question 90

questions.q: Name one war fought by the United States in the 1800s.
questions.explain: Also accepted: War of 1812; Civil War; Spanish-American War.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, B: 1800s, question 91

questions.q: Name the U.S. war between the North and the South.
questions.explain: The war between the North and the South was the Civil War.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, B: 1800s, question 92

questions.q: The Civil War had many important events. Name one.
questions.explain: Also accepted: (Battle of) Fort Sumter; Emancipation Proclamation; (Battle of) Vicksburg; Sherman’s March; (Surrender at) Appomattox; (Battle of) Antietam/Sharpsburg; Lincoln was assassinated.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, B: 1800s, question 93

questions.q: Abraham Lincoln is famous for many things. Name one.
options: First president of the United States
questions.explain: Also accepted: freed the slaves (Emancipation Proclamation); led the U.S. during the Civil War; 16th president of the United States; delivered the Gettysburg Address.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, B: 1800s, question 94 (* 65/20)

questions.q: What did the Emancipation Proclamation do?
options: Gave women the right to vote
Freed slaves in the Confederate states
questions.explain: Also accepted: freed the slaves; freed slaves in the Confederacy; freed slaves in most Southern states.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, B: 1800s, question 95

questions.q: What U.S. war ended slavery?
questions.explain: The Civil War ended slavery.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, B: 1800s, question 96

questions.q: What amendment says all persons born or naturalized in the United States, and subject to the jurisdiction thereof, are U.S. citizens?
questions.explain: The 14th Amendment (1868) defines U.S. citizenship.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, B: 1800s, question 97

questions.q: When did all men get the right to vote?
questions.explain: Also accepted: during Reconstruction; (with the) 15th Amendment; 1870.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, B: 1800s, question 98

questions.q: Name one leader of the women’s rights movement in the 1800s.
questions.explain: Also accepted: Elizabeth Cady Stanton; Sojourner Truth; Harriet Tubman; Lucretia Mott; Lucy Stone.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, B: 1800s, question 99

questions.q: Name one war fought by the United States in the 1900s.
questions.explain: Also accepted: World War I; Korean War; Vietnam War; (Persian) Gulf War.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 100

questions.q: Why did the United States enter World War I?
options: To force the Iraqi military from Kuwait
Because Germany attacked U.S. civilian ships
To stop the spread of communism
questions.explain: Also accepted: to support the Allied Powers (England, France, Italy, and Russia); to oppose the Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, the Ottoman Empire, and Bulgaria).
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 101

questions.q: When did all women get the right to vote?
questions.explain: Also accepted: after World War I; (with the) 19th Amendment.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 102

questions.q: What was the Great Depression?
options: A period of fast economic growth
The longest economic recession in modern history
A war between the North and the South
questions.explain: USCIS answer: longest economic recession in modern history.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 103

questions.q: When did the Great Depression start?
options: The attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941
The end of World War I in 1918
questions.explain: Also accepted: the Great Crash (1929).
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 104

questions.q: Who was president during the Great Depression and World War II?
questions.explain: (Franklin) Roosevelt was president during the Great Depression and World War II.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 105

questions.q: Why did the United States enter World War II?
options: To stop the spread of communism in Korea
questions.explain: Also accepted: (bombing of) Pearl Harbor; to support the Allied Powers (England, France, and Russia); to oppose the Axis Powers (Germany, Italy, and Japan).
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 106

questions.q: Dwight Eisenhower is famous for many things. Name one.
questions.explain: Also accepted: president at the end of (during) the Korean War; 34th president of the United States; signed the Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956 (created the Interstate System).
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 107

questions.q: Who was the United States’ main rival during the Cold War?
questions.explain: Also accepted: USSR; Russia.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 108

questions.q: During the Cold War, what was one main concern of the United States?
questions.explain: Also accepted: nuclear war.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 109

questions.q: Why did the United States enter the Korean War?
options: To stop the spread of communism
To force the Iraqi military from Kuwait
questions.explain: The U.S. entered the Korean War to stop the spread of communism.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 110

questions.q: Why did the United States enter the Vietnam War?
options: To stop the spread of communism
To respond to the September 11 attacks
questions.explain: The U.S. entered the Vietnam War to stop the spread of communism.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 111

questions.q: What did the civil rights movement do?
options: Fought to end the Cold War
questions.explain: The civil rights movement fought to end racial discrimination.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 112

questions.q: Martin Luther King, Jr. is famous for many things. Name one.
options: Led the Union army in the Civil War
questions.explain: Also accepted: worked for equality for all Americans; worked to ensure that people would “not be judged by the color of their skin, but by the content of their character.”
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 113 (* 65/20)

questions.q: Why did the United States enter the Persian Gulf War?
options: To respond to the September 11 attacks
To stop the spread of communism
To force the Iraqi military from Kuwait
questions.explain: The U.S. entered the Persian Gulf War (1991) to force the Iraqi military from Kuwait.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 114

questions.q: What major event happened on September 11, 2001 in the United States?
options: A major earthquake hit New York City
questions.explain: Also accepted: terrorists crashed two planes into the World Trade Center in New York City; a plane into the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia; and a plane aimed at Washington, D.C. crashed in a field in Pennsylvania.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 115 (* 65/20)

questions.q: Name one U.S. military conflict after the September 11, 2001 attacks.
questions.explain: Also accepted: (Global) War on Terror; War in Iraq. (The Persian Gulf War was in 1991.)
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 116

questions.q: Name one American Indian tribe in the United States.
questions.explain: The USCIS list includes Apache, Blackfeet, Cayuga, Cherokee, Cheyenne, Chippewa, Choctaw, Creek, Crow, Hopi, Huron, Inupiat, Lakota, Mohawk, Mohegan, Navajo, Oneida, Onondaga, Pueblo, Seminole, Seneca, Shawnee, Sioux, Teton, Tuscarora (full list at bia.gov). The Aztec, Inca and Maya were in Mexico, Central and South America.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 117

questions.q: Name one example of an American innovation.
questions.explain: Also accepted: light bulb; automobile (cars, internal combustion engine); skyscrapers; assembly line; landing on the moon; integrated circuit (IC).
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), American History, C: Recent American History and Other Important Historical Information, question 118

questions.q: What is the capital of the United States?
questions.explain: The capital of the United States is Washington, D.C.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), Symbols and Holidays, question 119

questions.q: Where is the Statue of Liberty?
questions.explain: Also accepted: New York; Liberty Island; New Jersey; near New York City; on the Hudson (River).
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), Symbols and Holidays, question 120

questions.q: Why does the flag have 13 stripes?
options: Because there are 13 amendments in the Bill of Rights
Because there were 13 presidents before Lincoln
questions.explain: Also accepted: (because the stripes) represent the original colonies.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), Symbols and Holidays, question 121 (* 65/20)

questions.q: Why does the flag have 50 stars?
options: One star for each Supreme Court justice
questions.explain: Also accepted: each star represents a state; (because there are) 50 states.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), Symbols and Holidays, question 122

questions.q: What is the name of the national anthem?
questions.explain: The national anthem is “The Star-Spangled Banner.”
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), Symbols and Holidays, question 123

questions.q: The Nation’s first motto was “E Pluribus Unum.” What does that mean?
questions.explain: Also accepted: we all become one.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), Symbols and Holidays, question 124

questions.q: What is Independence Day?
options: A holiday to celebrate U.S. independence from Britain
A holiday to honor soldiers who died in military service
A holiday to celebrate the end of the Civil War
questions.explain: Also accepted: the country’s birthday.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), Symbols and Holidays, question 125

questions.q: Name three national U.S. holidays.
options: Flag Day, Thanksgiving Day, Labor Day
Valentine’s Day, Memorial Day, New Year’s Day
Thanksgiving Day, Labor Day, Memorial Day
questions.explain: Accepted: New Year’s Day; Martin Luther King, Jr. Day; Presidents Day (Washington’s Birthday); Memorial Day; Juneteenth; Independence Day; Labor Day; Columbus Day; Veterans Day; Thanksgiving Day; Christmas Day. Flag Day, Halloween and Valentine’s Day are not federal holidays.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), Symbols and Holidays, question 126 (* 65/20)

questions.q: What is Memorial Day?
options: A holiday to celebrate U.S. independence
A holiday to honor U.S. presidents
A holiday to honor soldiers who died in military service
questions.explain: Memorial Day honors soldiers who died in military service.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), Symbols and Holidays, question 127

questions.q: What is Veterans Day?
options: A holiday to honor U.S. presidents
A holiday to celebrate the end of the Civil War
A holiday to honor people who have served in the U.S. military
questions.explain: Also accepted: a holiday to honor people in the (U.S.) military.
questions.ref: USCIS M-1778 (09/25) 128 Civics Questions and Answers (2025 version), Symbols and Holidays, question 128
